Alright, I've set up the basic HTML scaffold for the game and launched a simple Python HTTP server to serve it. The preview system reports that the document is fully loaded (readyState "complete") and the title is correct, with one canvas element present, which suggests that the Three.js script is at least being parsed and a WebGL canvas is being created.

However, when I try to capture a screenshot of the preview, it consistently times out after 30 seconds. That indicates that something in the rendering loop is either hanging, throwing an error that stops the frame from being drawn, or perhaps a modal dialog is blocking the render thread. The earlier attempt to hide an overlay element succeeded (the eval returned "hidden"), so UI elements aren't the issue.

I also attempted to measure FPS via a custom async eval that counts animation frames for a second, but that also timed out. If the rendering loop were running normally, that script would resolve quickly with an FPS estimate. The timeout suggests that requestAnimationFrame callbacks are never being invoked, likely because an uncaught exception halted the script before the render loop started.

The next logical step is to inspect any console output from the preview environment. The preview_console_logs tool can retrieve logs at various severity levels. Since I haven't seen any warnings or errors yet (the earlier call with level "warn" returned nothing), I should request all logs to capture any possible errors, warnings, or info messages that might have been emitted during script execution. This will give me insight into why the renderer is stuck and help me pinpoint the bug in the JavaScript code.

Therefore, I will invoke mcp__Claude_Preview__preview_console_logs with level "all" for the current server instance to retrieve the full console output.
